sheet-1-1.description: The left half of Sheet 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that the Pennsylvania Railroad (Trenton Division) runs straight up the page along its left side; north points to the upper left. The part covers the Roebling Village Annex east of the railroad and the strip of Florence Township south of Knickerbocker Way, west of Knickerbocker Pond. In the Annex, Railroad Avenue and Amboy Avenue run parallel to the tracks between Peace Street and Pond Street, lined by long rows of numbered two-storey brick dwellings backing onto a narrow central alley; a club and a hose cart house stand on the open block north of Peace Street, and a sewage pump house and a hose reel south of Pond Street. Knickerbocker Way crosses the sheet below the Annex, curving east past a garage for twenty cars toward the pond and the edge of the sheet. South of it, Olden Avenue and Norman Avenue are built up with stores and dwellings, many of them marked as stores with dwellings over, and with Hungarian and Slavic churches: the Magyar Reformed Church, St. Mary's Roman Catholic Church and the St. Nicholas Slavish Greek Catholic Church, the last two beside the curving street lettered Church. Further south, between Church and James Avenue, are two large concrete-block garages, a bakery and scattered frame dwellings. A high board fence follows the railroad, with the passenger depot beside the tracks. The strip of the sheet west of the railroad, showing 4th and 5th Avenues, South Street and the Roebling works, is masked out of this part because it is drawn out of position.
notes: Knickerbocker Way is today Hornberger Avenue.
Olden Avenue is today Alden Avenue.
The street lettered Church is today Roland Street.
James Avenue is today James Street.
Peace Street as drawn lies about 45 m south-west of today's Peace Street and was not used as control.
The railroad is today's River Line (NJ Transit).

map; 100 ft to an inch. Title sheet with index, key map and two map parts. Part 1 (left): Roebling Village Annex (Railroad Av., Amboy Av., Peace St., Pond St.) and Florence Township south of Knickerbocker Way (Olden Av., Norman Av., Church, James Av.), turned so that the railroad runs up the page; its strip west of the railroad (4th Av., 5th Av., South St., Roebling works blocks 22, 31, 32) is drawn about 30 m too close to the railroad and is masked out (sheets 2 and 3 cover it). Part 2 (lower right): Florence Township, Olden, Hamilton and Wallace Avenues with Wall St. and Cherry St. The key map (upper right, 500 ft to an inch) is not configured. Peace St. as drawn is about 45 m south-west of today's Peace Street and was left out. Old -> modern: Knickerbocker Way -> Hornberger Avenue, Olden Av. -> Alden Avenue, Church -> Roland Street, James Av. -> James Street, Wall -> 6th Street, unnamed street south of Cherry -> 7th Street.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: key map of the town (upper right), 500 ft to an inch (key map, not a to-scale sheet part).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip of part 1 west of the railroad (4th Av., 5th Av., South St., works blocks 22, 31, 32) (drawn about 30 m out of place relative to the rest of the part; masked out (shown on sheets 2 and 3)).

sheet-1-2.description: The lower right part of Sheet 1, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and set off from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line; its own north arrow points to the upper left. It shows a lightly built section of Florence Township south-west of Roebling village, laid out as a grid of large blocks with numbered lots. Olden Avenue runs down the left edge, with Hamilton Avenue and Wallace parallel to it, crossed by Wall and Cherry; an unnamed street that was not yet open runs diagonally across the top of the part, and another unnamed, unopened street crosses the bottom edge. Florence Road cuts across the lower right corner. Most lots are vacant or carry a single frame or concrete-block dwelling with a shed or garage; the Greek Catholic Church stands on Hamilton Avenue at Wall, and a bakery faces Hamilton Avenue north of it. Lot numbers run from about 101 to 130 along Wall and from 15 to 26 along Cherry and the bottom street. The large blocks numbered 55, 57, 58, 59 and 60 are mostly empty. The scale bar of the sheet (100 feet to one inch) and the Sanborn copyright line are printed in the lower right, and the legend key sits just above the part's upper boundary.
notes: Olden Avenue is today Alden Avenue.
Wall is today 6th Street.
The unnamed street south of Cherry (lettered Not Named, Not Open) is today 7th Street.
Florence Road is today Burlington-Bordentown Road.
Spruce Street and Pine Street, which today run between 6th Street, Cherry Street and 7th Street, are not drawn.

sheet-3-1.description: Sheet 3 at 100 feet to an inch covers the company village of Roebling built by John A. Roebling's Sons Co. beside the Delaware River. Riverside Avenue runs along the top beside Roebling Park and the river; below it Main and Knickerbocker Way cross the sheet, with South at the foot of the village, and the numbered avenues 2nd to 8th run up the page. The blocks are filled with uniform two-storey brick dwellings, single, double and in long rows, many with frame porches, on lots numbered along each avenue. Public and commercial buildings are concentrated near Main: the Roebling Inn on Riverside Avenue, a moving-picture theatre, a large general store with flour storage, offices, a hall, a barber, a cobbler and a drug store at 5th Avenue and Main, a bank, the post office, a Catholic church on the first floor of an office building and the public school on 4th Avenue. East of 2nd Avenue are the police station and jail, the fire department, a gate house and the company offices at the entrance to the works. Below Knickerbocker Way the blocks west of 6th Avenue are open, with a recreation hall, and the south-east corner holds company auto sheds, a gypsum-roofed concrete building, a carpenter shop and storage sheds on a curving siding. The Athletic Grounds lie west of 8th Avenue. The strip of the sheet south of South street, with the railroad, the P.R.R. freight house, coal storage, an ice house and Olden Avenue beyond the tracks, is left out of this annotation because it is drawn compressed, and an inset of the Roebling Public School in the lower left corner is not part of it either.
notes: Main is today Main Street.
Knickerbocker Way is today Hornberger Avenue; it is drawn about 12 m north of today's line relative to Main Street and South Street and was left out of the control.
South is today S Street.
Riverside Avenue junctions fit less well (up to about 5 m) than those on Main Street and South Street.

The strip south of South street (railroad, freight house, Olden Avenue, James Avenue, Church Street, Norman Avenue) is drawn compressed: the railroad would fall 20 to 35 m from today's River Line; it is masked out.

map; 100 ft to an inch. Roebling village: Riverside Av., Main, Knickerbocker Way and South streets, 2nd to 8th Avenues; Olden Av. along the railroad. Inset (lower left): Roebling Public School on Knickerbocker Way, not placed. Knickerbocker Way is drawn about 12 m north of today's Hornberger Avenue relative to Main Street and South Street (S Street), so Hornberger Avenue was left out of the fit. The strip south of South St. (blocks 23, 24, 27, 28, the P.R.R. freight house, coal storage, ice house, the railroad and the Olden Av. corner) is drawn compressed: the railroad falls 20 to 35 m from the River Line and Olden Av./James Av. about 40 m from today's junction; masked out of part 1.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Roebling Public School on Knickerbocker Way (no street junction (Knickerbocker Way, today Hornberger Avenue, only); needs position along Hornberger Avenue: the school building or a surviving lot corner).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip of part 1 south of South St. to the railroad and beyond (blocks 23, 24, 27, 28, P.R.R. freight house, coal storage, ice house, Olden Av., James Av.) (drawn compressed: the railroad would fall 20 to 35 m from its line; masked out (sheet 1 shows the railroad and Olden Av.); needs its own part with control on the railroad (carried from sheet-1-1) and South Street).
